FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 320
Committee: State Government Sponsor: Representative Chris Pringle
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 02/25/2025
House Bill 320 as introduced could decrease obligations of the state and local governments by
an undetermined amount dependent upon the difference in the cost of advertisement of certain
sealed contract bids on the website or digital version of a newspaper, as provided by this bill,
and the cost of advertisement otherwise required under current law.

FN-AREVHQS-4
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 320
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Sponsor: Representative Chris Pringle
Economic Development
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 04/17/2025
House Bill 320 as reported by the Committee on Fiscal Responsibility and Economic
Development would increase the obligations of the Department of Finance, by an undetermined
amount, to establish and maintain a centralized website or digital platform to provide publicly
accessible notice of advertisements for sealed bids. However, this increased obligation could be
offset, partly, by fees collected from awarding authorities for the privilege of posting
advertisements on the website. This could also increase or decrease the obligations of state and
local governments by an undetermined amount dependent upon the difference in the cost of
advertisement of certain sealed contract bids on the Department of Finance's centralized
website, or website or digital version of a newspaper, as provided by this bill, and the cost of
advertisement otherwise required under current law.
Additionally, this bill would create the12-member Study Commission of Public Notice of Title
39 Advertisements to study and make recommendations regarding the establishment,
maintenance, use, accessibility and promotion of the centralized website. This bill would
authorize members of the Commission to be reimbursed for necessary expenses associated with
attending meetings, which could increase the obligations of the various authorities of the
members by an undetermined amount dependent upon the extent to which members attend
meetings in person.
